name: Oholibamah
overview: Oholibamah was a male Edomite chief mentioned in Genesis 36:41. As a leader within the Edomite tribe, he held a position of authority among the descendants of Esau. Beyond his role as chief, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or notes about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Oholibamah means '[my] tent is a high place,' reflecting a proper name given in the Hebrew text of Genesis 36:41. This name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it carries a meaningful designation within the Edomite context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Oholibamah as a descendant of Esau, situating him within the Edomite lineage. No other family relationships or connections are recorded beyond this association.
scriptureSignificance: Oholibamah's significance lies in his role as a chief of Edom, representing the leadership among Esau's descendants. His mention in Genesis 36:41 highlights the established tribal structure and governance within the Edomite people. This contributes to the biblical understanding of the lineage and organization of nations descending from the patriarchs.
